THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation passed by the MACT II,
Vijayapura (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC.No.72/2010 dated 30.01.2019.
2.
Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted his arguments that the Tribunal has not awarded just and proper compensation, hence sought for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
3. As against this, learned counsel for the respondent/insurance company has submitted his arguments that judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is in accordance with law.
That there are no grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment.
Hence, sought for dismissal of the appeal.

4. On hearing the learned Advocates appearing for both parties, the following points would arise for consideration:
(1) Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper?
(2) What order?
5.

My answer to the above points are:
 (1) Partly affirmative  (2) As per final order  6.

I have gone through the impugned judgment and at paragraphs 16 to 18 the Tribunal has awarded the compensation by observing as under:
"16.
The Doctor examined before the Court as PW.4. PW-4 has given evidence before the Court and stated that x-ray film shows compression fracture of T- SESSIONS
JUne Doctor who treated the injured.
Admittedly, the 11 vertebra.
Doctor given disability certificate to the extent of 30 to 35% permanent disability to spine.
However, in his cross-examination he admitted that he has not mentioned the whole body disability.
Admittedly the Doctor who has given the disability certificate is not Ramgonda vs Nandakumar Raosaheb Patil And Anr on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63369097/

sentences.text: 2 injured

/ petitioner suffered compression fracture of T- 11 vertebra, then taking into consideration of age of the injured, Tribunal is of the opinion that there cannot be mere disability as stated by the Doctor.
Disability given is appears to be on higher side.
Admittedly, the disability is given to the spine and not for the whole body.
When the disability given is compared to the whole body, definitely it will come to lesser.

Taking into consideration of the compression fracture of T-11 vertebra and age of the injured, I am of the opinion that if 10% disability is taken total to the whole body it will meet ends of justice and equity.
Accordingly, this Tribunal comes to the conclusion that the injured has got 10% permanent disability when compared to the whole body for the injuries sustained in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
17. Injured stated that he is aged of 28 years no earning more than Rs.10,000/- per month by way of agricultural work.
Absolutely no documents are produced before the Court to show that injured is earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
Since age of the injured is shown as 35 years in the injury certificate Ex.P-31.
This Tribunal comes to the conclusion that age of the injured is 35 years as on the date and time of accident.
Since no acceptable documents are produced before the Court to show that injured is earning Rs. 10,000/- per month and taking into consideration of the year of accident i.e., on 12.11.2009.
This Tribunal is of the opinion that it is just and proper to consider the income of the injured at Rs.7000/- per month.
18. Income of the injured is taken into consideration @ 7000/- per month.
Then total annual income comes to Rs.84,000/-.
The proper multiplier applicable to the injured is 16.

If monthly income of Rs.84,000/- is multiplied by 16, it will comes to Rs.
13,44,000/- and 10% of the same comes to the Rs. 1,34,400/-.
Hence, an amount of Rs. 1,34,400/- is awarded towards Loss of Future Income of the injured for the injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
Hence, this Tribunal comes to the conclusion that petitioner is entitled for following compensation for the injuries suffered by him in the Motor Vehicle accident.

Details of Compensation Sl. Name of the Head Amount (in Rs.) No.
1. Loss of Future 1,34,400/-
Income 2. Medical Expenses 10,000/-

3. Attendant Charges 5,000/-
4. Pain and Suffering 50,000/-

Loss of Amenities 20,000/-
6. Loss of earning during treatment 21,000/-
 period  T O T A L: 2,40,400/-
 (Rupees Two  Lakhs Forth  Thousand Four  Hundred only)
7.

A perusal of finding given by the Tribunal, it reveals that the Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities instead of Rs.30,000/- and towards attendant charges are concerned, Tribunal has awarded only Rs.5,000/- and as such same is enhanced to Rs.8,000/-.
8. Tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards food, diet, nourishment and conveyance charges.
As such a sum of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards same.
9. Accordingly claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.2,58,400/- as against Rs.2,40,400/-.

10. In view of the above, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
(a) The appeal is allowed in part.
(b) The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.72/2010 dated 30.01.2019 is modified.

(c) The compensation of Rs.2,40,400/-
awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.2,58,400/-.

(d) The insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the claimant along with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
